findings.text: Create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app in the developer console.
findings.quote: In the Developer console, select the Create dropdown and choose OAuth 2.0 integration to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.

findings.text: Choose between account-level or resource-level grants.
findings.quote: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, you can choose between two grant types: Account-level grant: The user’s consent applies at the Atlassian account level. Resource-level grant: The user’s consent is limited to the specific site(s) they select on the consent screen.

findings.text: Navigate to the developer console to create an app.
findings.quote: From any page on developer.atlassian.com, select your profile icon in the top-right corner, and from the dropdown, select Developer console.

findings.text: Configure the OAuth 2.0 (3LO) settings.
findings.quote: Select Authorization in the left menu. Next to OAuth 2.0 (3LO), select Configure.

findings.text: Add the required callback URL.
findings.quote: Enter the Callback URL. Set this to any URL that is accessible by the app. When you implement OAuth 2.0 (3LO) in your app (see next section), the redirect_uri must match this URL.

findings.text: Add APIs to the app.
findings.quote: Select Permissions in the left menu. Next to the API you want to add, select Add.

findings.text: The authorization endpoint is used to start the flow.
findings.quote: https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize?

findings.text: The token endpoint is used to exchange the code for a token.
findings.quote: https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token

findings.text: Only the code grant flow is supported.
findings.quote: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) currently supports the code grant flow only. It does not support the implicit grant flow.

findings.text: Apps cannot be deleted if they are installed.
findings.quote: You can only delete an app if it's not installed anywhere. If your app is currently installed on a site, uninstall it.

findings.text: Apps are private by default.
findings.quote: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, it's private by default. This means that only you can install and use it.

findings.text: Register your application in Jira by creating an incoming link in application links.
findings.quote: Register your application in Jira by creating an incoming link in application links.

findings.text: Jira supports Authorization code with PKCE and Authorization code flows.
findings.quote:
We support the following OAuth 2.0 flows:

Authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)

Authorization code

findings.text: The authorization endpoint is /rest/oauth2/latest/authorize.
findings.quote: Request authorization code by redirecting the user to the /rest/oauth2/latest/authorize page with the following query parameters:

findings.text: The token endpoint is /rest/oauth2/latest/token.
findings.quote: curl -X POST https://atlassian.example.com/rest/oauth2/latest/token?client_id=CLIENT_ID&client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET&code=CODE&grant_type=authorization_code&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&code_verifier=CODE_VERIFIER

findings.text: PKCE is supported for the authorization code flow.
findings.quote: Authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)

findings.text: Access tokens expire in 7200 seconds.
findings.quote: "expires_in": 7200,

findings.quote: Register your application in Jira by creating an incoming link in application links. After creating the link, you should receive the OAuth credentials: Client ID and Client secret

findings.text: Apps not reviewed by Atlassian will show a warning to users.
findings.quote: Users trying to install an unapproved OAuth 2.0 integration are warned that the app has not yet been reviewed by Atlassian.

findings.text: OAuth 2.0 apps are private by default when created.

findings.text: You must enable sharing to distribute your app to other users.
findings.quote: If you want to distribute your app to other users, you must enable sharing.

findings.text: Marketplace support typically responds to app approval submissions in 5 to 10 business days.
findings.quote: Typically you should hear from a support member in 5 - 10 business days.

findings.text: Atlassian does not impose a limit on the number of users for an OAuth app.
findings.quote: Atlassian will not limit by users.

findings.text: Create an OAuth App in the developer console.
findings.quote: Create an OAuth App in the developer console. Make sure to select the scopes you intend to call in Jira.

findings.text: Construct an authorization URL with a state parameter.
findings.quote: Now construct an authorization URL. If you are in the Authorization screen of the Console, then you may see an example URL already. You only need to set a value for the state parameter.

findings.text: Exchange the authorization code for an access token.
findings.quote: On the back-end (curl or Postman), exchange the authorization code for an access token.

findings.text: Use the access token to call the Jira REST API.
findings.quote: Then use the access token to call the Jira REST API. You’ll see the access token acted “as you”, even though you never provided your credentials to the HTTP client.

findings.text: The authorization URL requires the prompt parameter to be set to consent.
findings.quote: prompt=consent

findings.text: The authorization flow uses the authorization code grant type.
findings.quote: Atlassian’s OAuth (as implemented with authorization code grants only) is not the appropriate option.

findings.text: Use a shared service account email for the Atlassian account owning the OAuth app.
findings.quote: I strongly recommend using a shared “service account”. There’s no special way to create that for Atlassian, but just use an email alias where group membership can be managed.

findings.text: The approval process for apps takes 10-15 business days.
findings.quote: Approvals take 10-15 business days, but approval times vary depending on current volume and the Marketplace team’s availability.

findings.text: Apps that break the host Atlassian app UI will be rejected.
findings.quote: Doesn't break the host Atlassian app UI: The UI of the host Atlassian app should be functional and intact when your app is installed. If the UI breaks, your app will be rejected.

findings.text: Trademark infringement results in an automatic rejection.
findings.quote: Doesn't infringe Atlassian trademarks: Trademark infringement is an automatic rejection, so be sure to read our brand guidelines for Marketplace Partners before submitting your app.

findings.text: Using personal or generic email domains for paid-via-Atlassian apps is not permitted.
findings.quote: Personal or generic domains (like Gmail or Yahoo) are not permitted for paid-via-Atlassian apps. The email must clearly match the submitting organization and be active for business use.

findings.text: Public approved apps must not use Basic authentication.
findings.quote: Whilst your app may make use of Basic authentication with Atlassian's product REST APIs for ease of development/speed during development, this shall not be the case for any public, approved app.
